public_rationale: New York's companion-chatbot safeguards took effect on November 5, two weeks before the post. They required suicide and self-harm detection protocols and crisis-service referrals, backed by enforcement. That contradicts the categorical claim that these bots had no regulation. It does not establish comprehensive national coverage or effective prevention of every harmful response.
limitations: The counterexample concerns covered AI companions operating in New York.
Legal requirements and their practical effectiveness are separate questions.
The decisive source is an official government implementation announcement.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Unlike airlines, cars, and bakeries, AI chatbots that tell kids to kill themselves are not subject to regulation.

statement.excerpt: Airlines have regulations, cars have regulations, bakeries have regulations; AI bots that tell kids to kill themselves don’t.
statement.document_title: Mayday: The White House is attempting to circumvent Congress and crush the rights of individual states to regulate AI.

from_speaker: AI bots that tell kids to kill themselves
Airlines have regulations, cars have regulations, bakeries have regulations
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that no applicable U.S. regulation specifically addressed chatbots' interactions involving children or suicide and self-harm.
A binding state requirement governing covered companion chatbots suffices to contradict the categorical absence claim.
The statement does not require that every chatbot be covered or that existing rules successfully prevent every harmful interaction.
The target is the legal position at publication, reconstructed from laws and effective-date records through November 19, 2025; no beginning date is specified.
criteria.support_condition: No federal or state requirement in force by publication specifically regulated the relevant chatbot interactions or self-harm safeguards.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one applicable federal or state requirement governing such chatbot interactions or self-harm safeguards was already in force.

evidence.explanation: The official notice says that, effective November 5, covered AI companions must detect suicidal ideation or self-harm and direct users to crisis services. These enforceable requirements applied before Marcus's post and directly address the relevant chatbot risk.
